[IDAT.2.3.2] Because the return type is a pair rather than a scalar
([IDAT.2.3.1]), every return site would otherwise spell out a compound
literal. Two macros keep that from drowning the code: one names the success
value, which carries no detail and is by far the most common thing any
function returns, and one pairs a status with a detail string.

They are a convenience of this implementation, not part of the contract. What
crosses the boundary is the value; how a call site spelled it is invisible to
the caller.
